spatial_accessibility_rule: Any visual board edge or layout must also render as a labelled linear relation list: source entity → relation → target entity → passage → confidence/TX1.

repair_metadata.note: Only duplicate-book surface artifacts, if any, were normalized.

records.label: Baptism and temptation — witness boundaries
records.scope: Jesus' baptism, temptation, and Johannine baptism testimony without harmonizing witness details.
records.chronology_claim: Matthew and Luke give different local orders for the second and third detailed temptations; a merged single order should not be presented as T1 for both.
records.nonvisual_equivalent: Preserve Matthew's local order and Luke's local order separately; any harmonized master order is a reconstruction, not a direct statement shared by both.

records.label: Calling disciples — distinct scenes and names
records.scope: Synoptic fishermen calls and John 1 disciple-calling material kept as distinct witness scenes.
records.chronology_claim: John 1 and the Synoptic fishermen-call passages contain distinct narrated scenes; the project must not force a single exhaustive chronology from them.
records.nonvisual_equivalent: Treat each witness's local sequence as direct evidence and any merged chronology as a reconstruction requiring explicit uncertainty.

records.label: Paralytic and authority — Synoptic parallel with Johannine contrast
records.scope: Matthew/Mark/Luke paralytic parallel, contrasted with John 5 without claiming the Johannine healing is the same event.
records.chronology_claim: John 5 has overlapping motifs (healing, mat) but a different setting and controversy; similarity is insufficient to merge the scenes.
records.nonvisual_equivalent: Keep John 5 as CONTRAST_NOT_PARALLEL and the Synoptic roof-paralytic event as its own parallel set.

records.label: Jairus and the bleeding woman — intercalated witness comparison
records.scope: Matthew/Mark/Luke Jairus-and-woman narratives, contrasted with John 4 without false event identity.
records.chronology_claim: Matthew begins with the daughter already described as dead, while Mark and Luke begin with her dying and later report her death; each local narrative sequence must remain distinct.
records.nonvisual_equivalent: Preserve Matthew's local statement and Mark/Luke's local progression; do not rewrite one witness to match another.

records.label: Feeding the five thousand — four witness profiles
records.scope: Feeding narrative with witness-specific details and direct comparison.
records.chronology_claim: The feeding accounts can be compared directly, but signature details such as Philip's test, the boy with barley loaves, groups of hundreds/fifties, and 'besides women and children' remain witness-local.
records.nonvisual_equivalent: Treat the shared provision/count claims as T2 comparison while preserving each witness-local detail.

records.label: Walking on the sea — three narratives and a Luke boundary
records.scope: Matthew, Mark, and John walking-on-water narratives; Luke is an explicit no-direct-parallel boundary in the assigned scope.
records.chronology_claim: Mark says the boat was to go toward Bethsaida, while John says the disciples went toward Capernaum; a single reconstructed route should not be mislabeled as a shared T1 statement.
records.nonvisual_equivalent: Preserve each witness's destination wording; any detailed geographic reconciliation is reconstruction rather than direct shared wording.

records.label: Confession and transfiguration — Synoptic sequence with Johannine contrast
records.scope: Synoptic confession/transfiguration comparison, with John 12 heavenly-voice material kept as a distinct contrast rather than harmonized.
records.chronology_claim: Matthew/Mark say 'after six days' while Luke says 'about eight days'; the project must preserve both local sequence expressions rather than force a single T1 day count.
records.nonvisual_equivalent: Both local expressions are direct witness statements; a single harmonized exact interval is not established as one shared wording.

records.label: Entry into Jerusalem — witness-specific signs and words
records.scope: Entry narratives compared without transferring distinctive animals, acclamations, reactions, or retrospective comments.
records.chronology_claim: Mark explicitly places a temple look-around and return to Bethany after the entry before the next day's temple action; project display order must preserve that Mark-local sequence.
records.nonvisual_equivalent: Mark's local sequence is T1 for Mark; cross-Gospel display order is not automatically a shared T1 chronology.

records.label: Temple actions — Synoptic placement and John 2 boundary
records.scope: Temple actions compared while refusing to force John 2 and the Synoptic temple episodes into one historical event.
records.chronology_claim: Whether John 2 and the Synoptic final-week temple action represent one historical event relocated literarily or two actions is not responsibly forced into a single canonical answer by these texts alone.
records.nonvisual_equivalent: Keep John 2 and the Synoptic final-week scenes as separately attested narrative placements; any historical identification is D1/reconstruction.

records.label: Roman trial distinctions — Pilate, Herod, Barabbas, and witness-local scenes
records.scope: Roman trial narratives with each witness's dialogue, actors, sequence, and place terminology kept separate.
records.chronology_claim: The four trial narratives have overlapping but non-identical scene structure; a project display sequence cannot be labeled a single T1 transcript of every witness.
records.nonvisual_equivalent: Use witness-local sequence for T1 claims; use T2 only for direct comparisons; merged trial reconstruction remains explicitly a reconstruction.

records.label: Crucifixion distinctions — sayings, signs, witnesses, and TX1
records.scope: Crucifixion narratives compared with witness-local sayings and signs; Luke 23:34a is TX1-sensitive.
records.chronology_claim: Mark's third-hour crucifixion statement and John's trial-day timing cannot be collapsed by this content lane into one forced T1 clock reconstruction.
records.nonvisual_equivalent: Preserve each local time statement; any detailed harmonization of clock systems or exact merged timing is D1 and outside direct-text grading.

records.label: Burial distinctions — Joseph, tomb witnesses, spices, and guards
records.scope: Burial narratives with named people and actions kept within each Gospel witness.
records.chronology_claim: The burial narratives can be directly compared for stated actions, but the complete merged order of all women, Nicodemus, guard arrangements, and spice preparation is a reconstruction rather than one witness's T1 sequence.
records.nonvisual_equivalent: Grade each witness-local sequence directly; mark merged synthesis as comparison/reconstruction.

records.label: Resurrection discovery — empty-tomb witness boundaries
records.scope: First discovery narratives compared without importing named women, messenger counts, destinations, or dialogue.
records.chronology_claim: The witnesses narrate different selections and ordering of women, messengers, disciple visits, and appearances; a single exhaustive merged discovery timeline is not a T1 statement of any one Gospel.
records.nonvisual_equivalent: Preserve local sequences; comparisons are T2; any exhaustive harmonized discovery sequence is D1 reconstruction.

records.label: Resurrection appearances — distinct scenes and Mark longer-ending TX1
records.scope: Major post-resurrection appearance scenes compared without forcing one exhaustive appearance order; Mark 16:9–20 is explicitly TX1-sensitive.
records.chronology_claim: No one Gospel supplies a complete merged ordering of every appearance found across all four witness corpora, and Mark's longer ending itself has a major textual-transmission boundary.
records.nonvisual_equivalent: Preserve each witness-local appearance order; cross-witness exhaustive ordering is D1, with TX1 attached wherever Mark 16:9–20 participates.

records.label: Commission and closing narratives — distinct commands, locations, and endings
records.scope: Commission/sending material compared without flattening commands or locations; Mark 16:15–20 is TX1-sensitive.
records.chronology_claim: Matthew's Galilee mountain, Luke's Jerusalem/Bethany closing sequence, John's John 20 and John 21 scenes, and the Mark longer ending should not be forced into one T1 commission chronology.
records.nonvisual_equivalent: Keep each commission scene local; merged sequencing is D1; Mark 16:15–20 remains TX1 wherever used.
